draft.title: Viking society and beliefs
card: Jarl
a wealthy noble who held land and power. Jarls led warriors and often ruled a region.
Free farmer
a person who owned or worked land and was not enslaved. Free farmers made up much of Viking society and could speak at the local assembly.
Thrall
an enslaved person, often captured in raids or born to enslaved parents. Thralls did hard work and had few rights.
Disputes were settled at the thing, a local assembly of free people. Vikings worshipped many gods, such as Odin and Thor.
draft.remember: Viking people ranked as jarls, free farmers or thralls. The thing settled disputes, and many gods were worshipped.

a.q: In Viking society, which group was enslaved?
opts: Thralls
Jarls
Free farmers
Members of the thing
a.why: Thralls were enslaved and had few rights. Jarls were powerful nobles and free farmers were not enslaved. The thing was an assembly, not a social group.
a.clue: Think about who had few rights and did hard work.

b.q: Two farmers in Iceland argue over who owns a flock of sheep. In Viking society, how would the dispute most likely be settled?
opts: At the thing, the local assembly
By the Viking king alone, in private
By asking the thralls to decide
By a priest of Odin, who ruled all disputes
b.why: The thing was the local assembly where free people settled disputes. The other options give the decision to one person or to thralls, and the card says none of these settled disputes.

b.best: At the thing, the local assembly

problems.detail: Why (b) says 'the card says none of these settled disputes', but the card never says this. It only says disputes were settled at the thing. Better: 'The card says disputes were settled at the thing, not by one person or by thralls.'

check.summary: The card and both questions are accurate, and each question has one clear answer. The only problem is that the explanation for question b claims the card says something it does not.
